prerequisites: Courses from the Bachelor's program in chemical technology (separation processes, reactor technology, ...)

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze processes in chemical technology with an emphasis on key themes.
Acquire knowledge of techniques relevant to chemical technologists and apply those techniques.
Define research questions and choose methods.
Design and execute an experimental study.
Perform quantitative calculations and computer simulations.
Critically reflect on own findings regarding intended objectives, sustainability, and applicability.
Learn to work with software for data analysis, simulation, and optimization.
Awareness of a circular economy, sustainability, safety.

syllabus_topics: Integrated year project within thematic areas focused on innovation, environment, energy, and/or sustainable developments in the (bio)chemical industry.

Examples of themes: design of modern surface layers, extraction and encapsulation of biomolecules, bio-based chemical technology, waste processing and circular economy, alternatives to disposable plastic.
Information sessions on thematic areas, experimental and computational techniques, lab safety, literature review, and scientific writing in English.
Defining general project goals and specific research questions.
Applying various aspects of chemical technology (e.g., reactor processes, separation processes, analytical techniques, simulation and optimization, thermodynamic concepts, rheology).
Proposing project goal and research plan & discussion with course coordinators and daily supervisors.
Writing a review article on the domain or a specific aspect of the identified project.
Short report on the project status (end of first semester).
Feedback and guidance by course coordinators and daily supervisors (beginning of second semester).
Writing a scientific article about the project results.
Presentation of project results to a broader audience.
teaching_methods: Information sessions (analytical techniques, setting up experiments, scientific writing in English, safety)
Performing experiments in didactic and research laboratories
Data analysis, simulation and process optimization using software (e.g., Matlab, Aspen Plus)

assessment_methods.method: Proposing project goal and research plan & discussion with course coordinators and daily supervisors
Review article on the domain or a specific aspect of the identified project
Peer assessment of first semester activities
Scientific article about the project results
Presentation of the project results to a broader public
Peer assessment of second semester activities
Project content (e.g. creativity, depth, correctness of applied methods, integration of various experimental and/or computational techniques)

assessment_rules: The permanent evaluation consists of several components. Formal feedback is provided for the review and scientific articles, and peer assessment results are communicated qualitatively. The technical-scientific quality of the final result is always decisive in determining the final score. Unauthorized prolonged absence and/or irresponsible intentional unsafe behavior results in a 0/20 for this course. Due to the specific evaluation format, no alternative exam is organized in the September examination period.
